one-check-per-line.why: all 5 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 5

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "Running `node src/app.js <tmp>/c.json`, where c.json contains the four lines `{`"

words-only.why: I compared the PASS and FAIL conditions of all five verifier checks with the words of their expect lines. Check 1 tests only "exit code is 1 and stdout ... is empty". Check 2 tests only `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json" path, and line 3 and column 3 "in some readable form", so it does not require exact wording. Check 3 tests only that the call throws and the message includes the path. Check 4 tests `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and deepEqual to {port: 9000}, which matches "returns { port: 9000 }". Check 5 tests that `npm test` passes at the PR head and that at least one test checking the file path fails against base src. The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": line and column computed from the file text rather than Node's message, SyntaxError, cause, ENOENT, the path not being resolved, and the README. None of these appear in a PASS or FAIL condition.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository: src/app.js, src/config.js, test/config.test.js, and the `npm test` script (`node --test`). The builder's step 6 commands are valid shell. `mktemp -d`, the printf escapes and `node src/app.js $d/c.json` are fine, and `$d` is reused within the same session. In the verifier brief, checks 1–4 use valid shell. The `node --input-type=module -e` snippets have valid ESM syntax: the `{loadConfig}` named import is the same one the issue's own proofs use, and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'` is a real module. `wc -c < $d/out` and the grep -F calls are valid. Check 5 uses `git merge-base HEAD <the PR's target ref>`, a placeholder the verifier fills in. After that, `git checkout B -- src && npm test; git checkout HEAD -- src` restores the tree. The spawnSync/process.execPath suggestion is a real Node API. I found no command that names a missing file or tool, or has bad syntax.

catches-traps.why: Item 1: The builder brief says "Do NOT make `loadConfig` swallow the error or return `{}`/defaults." This fully covers it. Item 2: Builder step 1 says to throw a new error, with "a SyntaxError is a good choice, so the existing test `bad JSON throws` that asserts `SyntaxError` still passes". That sentence doesn't name the file. But "Relevant files" names `test/config.test.js` as the node:test file, and step 4 adds tests to that file. So the brief points to the test and its SyntaxError assertion. It also makes clear that wrapping the error in a non-SyntaxError type would break that test. The verifier's advisory section repeats the point ("the original `bad JSON throws` test asserts that"). Both items are handled.

avoids-must-not.why:
I checked both must_not items against both briefs, and neither brief breaks them.

Item 1: the builder brief does have the builder wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch. But the catch must "throw a new error … whose `message` includes the path". The brief also says explicitly: "Do NOT make `loadConfig` swallow the error or return `{}`/defaults." So the error is caught only to be thrown again, never to return a value.

Item 2: verifier Check 2 passes when stderr shows `bad config:`, the exact path, and line 3 and column 3 "in some readable form (e.g. `line 3 column 3`, `3:3`, `line 3, col 3`)". It fails only when one of those pieces is missing, not because the wording or order differs from one fixed format.

Nothing else in either brief matches the must_not list.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with each verifier check. The builder brief has no PASS or FAIL conditions, and it doesn't include Check 3's `node --input-type=module` probe, Check 4's deepEqual script, Check 5's merge-base/`git checkout B -- src` step, or the grep commands. Step 6's hand checks (`printf '{\n  "port": 9000,...' > $d/c.json; node src/app.js $d/c.json`, the ok.json run, `npm test`) are commands the issue's proofs 1 and 4 name, which the criterion allows. Step 4 tells the builder to write its own tests using inputs from the expect lines, which is also allowed. Step 3 ("must still return `{ port: 9000 }`") and step 2's "line 3 and column 3" repeat the expect lines, so they set the bar rather than copy the checker's method. Step 2 tells the builder to compute line and column itself, which matches an advisory note in the verifier brief, but that note is not a pass or fail condition or a probe. The criterion holds for the whole brief.
